ActionConstraint._: Plays a saved Action (an animation clip) and picks the frame from how much the target moves, rotates or scales, so one object's motion drives another animation.
ActionConstraint.owner_space: Which coordinate system the constrained object (the owner) is measured in. World is the scene grid, Local is the object's own axes.
ActionConstraint.owner_space.WORLD: Use the world grid, the same for every object in the scene.
ActionConstraint.owner_space.CUSTOM: Use the axes of another object, bone or vertex group that you pick.
ActionConstraint.owner_space.POSE: Armature bones only: use the pose space and ignore the armature object's own move/rotate/scale.
ActionConstraint.owner_space.LOCAL_WITH_PARENT: Bones: local to the bone's rest pose, but still including whatever its parent adds.
ActionConstraint.owner_space.LOCAL: Use the owner's own axes, so 'X' means along the object's own X direction.
ActionConstraint.target_space: Which coordinate system the target is read in. This decides what 'the target's X' means before it is copied or used.
ActionConstraint.target_space.WORLD: Read the target using the world grid.
ActionConstraint.target_space.CUSTOM: Read the target using the axes of another object, bone or vertex group you pick.
ActionConstraint.target_space.POSE: Armature bones only: read the target in pose space and ignore the armature object's own transform.
ActionConstraint.target_space.LOCAL_WITH_PARENT: Bones: read the target in its rest-pose local space, still including its parent's effect.
ActionConstraint.target_space.LOCAL: Read the target using its own axes.
ActionConstraint.target_space.LOCAL_OWNER_ORIENT: Local space plus a fix for the owner and target bones resting at different angles, so they move the same way.
ActionConstraint.space_subtarget: The bone, or vertex group, whose axes are used when a Custom space is chosen. Leave empty to use the object itself.
ActionConstraint.mute: Switch this constraint off without deleting it. Handy for quickly seeing what it does.
ActionConstraint.enabled: Turns the constraint's result on or off. Off means Blender ignores it completely.
ActionConstraint.show_expanded: Open or fold this constraint's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
ActionConstraint.active: Marks this as the constraint you are currently editing in the stack.
ActionConstraint.influence: How strongly the constraint applies. 0 means no effect, 1 means full effect, in between blends the two.
ActionConstraint.subtarget: The specific bone, or vertex group, on the target to use. Leave empty to use the whole target object.
ActionConstraint.mix_mode: How the action's result is combined with the owner's own transform. Replace ignores the owner's transform, the other modes stack them.
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.REPLACE: Throw away the owner's own transform and use only what the action produces.
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.BEFORE_FULL: Action goes first, then the owner's transform is applied on top, combined as plain full matrices.
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.BEFORE: Action acts like a parent of the owner, with scale inherited in the aligned way (no shearing).
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.BEFORE_SPLIT: Action goes first, but location, rotation and scale are each combined separately.
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.AFTER_FULL: Owner's transform goes first, then the action is applied on top, combined as plain full matrices.
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.AFTER: Action acts like a child of the owner, with scale inherited in the aligned way (no shearing).
ActionConstraint.mix_mode.AFTER_SPLIT: Action goes after the owner's transform, but location, rotation and scale are each combined separately.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel: Which movement of the target (position, rotation or scale on one axis) decides the frame of the action that plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.LOCATION_X: The target's position on the X axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.LOCATION_Y: The target's position on the Y axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.LOCATION_Z: The target's position on the Z axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.ROTATION_X: The target's rotation on the X axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.ROTATION_Y: The target's rotation on the Y axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.ROTATION_Z: The target's rotation on the Z axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.SCALE_X: The target's scale on the X axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.SCALE_Y: The target's scale on the Y axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.transform_channel.SCALE_Z: The target's scale on the Z axis drives which frame of the action plays.
ActionConstraint.action_slot_handle: Internal number that picks which slot (sub-part) of the Action this constraint plays. You normally set it with the Slot dropdown.
ActionConstraint.last_slot_identifier: Name of the slot used last, remembered so Blender can reconnect to it if you swap the action.
ActionConstraint.use_bone_object_action: Bones only: use the object-level animation channels of the action on this bone, instead of the bone's own channels.
ActionConstraint.frame_start: First frame of the action to use. The target's Min value maps to this frame.
ActionConstraint.frame_end: Last frame of the action to use. The target's Max value maps to this frame.
ActionConstraint.max: The highest target value that counts. When the target reaches it, the action is at its End Frame.
ActionConstraint.min: The lowest target value that counts. When the target is at it, the action is at its Start Frame.
ActionConstraint.eval_time: Scrub through the action by hand: 0 is the start frame, 1 is the end frame. Needs Use Evaluation Time on.
ActionConstraint.use_eval_time: Pick the action frame with the Evaluation Time slider instead of from the target's movement.

ArmatureModifier.show_expanded: Open or fold this modifier's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
ArmatureModifier.is_active: Marks this as the modifier you are currently working on in the stack.
ArmatureModifier.use_pin_to_last: Keeps this modifier locked at the bottom of the stack, so newly added modifiers go above it.
ArmatureModifier.use_apply_on_spline: Applies this modifier, and the deforming ones above it, to the curve's control points instead of the finished shape.
ArmatureModifier.use_bone_envelopes: Use each bone's envelope (its zone of influence) to decide which points it moves.
ArmatureModifier.use_vertex_groups: Use vertex groups named after bones to decide which points each bone moves. This is the usual way.
ArmatureModifier.use_deform_preserve_volume: Keeps volume when bones twist, so joints don't pinch like a squeezed candy wrapper. Blends rotations as quaternions.
ArmatureModifier.use_multi_modifier: Use the same starting shape as the modifier before it, and mix both results using the overall vertex group. For stacking armatures.
ArmatureModifier.vertex_group: Optional vertex group that controls strength point by point. Heavier weight means stronger effect, empty means everywhere.
ArmatureModifier.invert_vertex_group: Flip the vertex group, so painted areas are ignored and unpainted areas are affected.

ArrayModifier.show_viewport: Show the modifier's effect in the 3D viewport. Turn it off if the viewport feels slow.
ArrayModifier.show_render: Use the modifier when you render the final image. Off means renders ignore it.
ArrayModifier.show_in_editmode: Show the modifier's result while you edit the mesh or shape in Edit Mode.
ArrayModifier.show_on_cage: Edit Mode only: lets you grab and move the modified result directly instead of the original points.
ArrayModifier.show_expanded: Open or fold this modifier's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
ArrayModifier.is_active: Marks this as the modifier you are currently working on in the stack.
ArrayModifier.use_pin_to_last: Keeps this modifier locked at the bottom of the stack, so newly added modifiers go above it.
ArrayModifier.use_apply_on_spline: Applies this modifier, and the deforming ones above it, to the curve's control points instead of the finished shape.
ArrayModifier.fit_type: How Blender decides how many copies to make: a fixed number, a total length, or the length of a curve.
ArrayModifier.fit_type.FIXED_COUNT: Make exactly the number of copies set in Count.
ArrayModifier.fit_type.FIT_LENGTH: Make as many copies as fit inside the Length you set.
ArrayModifier.fit_type.FIT_CURVE: Make as many copies as fit along a curve object.
ArrayModifier.count: How many copies in total, including the original. Higher means a longer chain.
ArrayModifier.fit_length: The total length the copies should fill. Bigger length means more copies fit.
ArrayModifier.use_constant_offset: Shift each copy by a fixed distance that you type in.
ArrayModifier.constant_offset_displace: The fixed distance between copies on X, Y and Z, measured in scene units (usually meters).
ArrayModifier.use_relative_offset: Shift each copy by a multiple of the object's own size, so copies line up next to each other.
ArrayModifier.relative_offset_displace: Gap between copies as a fraction of the object's size. 1 puts them side by side, 2 leaves one object-width of gap.
ArrayModifier.use_merge_vertices: Weld points of neighboring copies that are close together, joining them into one connected shape.
ArrayModifier.use_merge_vertices_cap: Also weld the first and last copies together, which closes the chain into a ring.
ArrayModifier.merge_threshold: How close two points must be to get welded. Low is strict, high merges points that are further apart.
ArrayModifier.use_object_offset: Also shift each copy by the position of another object, so you can move or rotate that object to shape the array.
ArrayModifier.offset_u: Slides the texture of each copy sideways (U direction) so the pattern continues across copies.
ArrayModifier.offset_v: Slides the texture of each copy up/down (V direction) so the pattern continues across copies.

BevelModifier._: Rounds off or chamfers sharp edges and corners, so they catch light the way real objects do.
BevelModifier.show_viewport: Show the modifier's effect in the 3D viewport. Turn it off if the viewport feels slow.
BevelModifier.show_render: Use the modifier when you render the final image. Off means renders ignore it.
BevelModifier.show_in_editmode: Show the modifier's result while you edit the mesh or shape in Edit Mode.
BevelModifier.show_on_cage: Edit Mode only: lets you grab and move the modified result directly instead of the original points.
BevelModifier.show_expanded: Open or fold this modifier's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
BevelModifier.is_active: Marks this as the modifier you are currently working on in the stack.
BevelModifier.use_pin_to_last: Keeps this modifier locked at the bottom of the stack, so newly added modifiers go above it.
BevelModifier.use_apply_on_spline: Applies this modifier, and the deforming ones above it, to the curve's control points instead of the finished shape.
BevelModifier.width: How big the bevel is. Low gives a tiny soft edge, high gives a big rounded edge.
BevelModifier.width_pct: Bevel size as a percentage of the neighboring edges. Only used with the Percent width type.
BevelModifier.segments: How many slices make up the rounded edge. 1 is a flat chamfer, higher is smoother and heavier.
BevelModifier.affect: Whether to bevel edges (the lines between faces) or only vertices (the corner points).
BevelModifier.limit_method: Which parts of the mesh get beveled.
BevelModifier.limit_method.NONE: Bevel everything by the same amount.
BevelModifier.limit_method.ANGLE: Only bevel edges where two faces meet at a sharp enough angle.
BevelModifier.limit_method.WEIGHT: Bevel edges based on a painted weight, so you choose which edges and how much.
BevelModifier.limit_method.VGROUP: Bevel only where the vertex group weights say so.
BevelModifier.edge_weight: Name of the edge attribute holding the bevel weights (used by the Weight limit method).
BevelModifier.vertex_weight: Name of the vertex attribute holding the bevel weights (used by the Weight limit method).
BevelModifier.angle_limit: Edges sharper than this angle get beveled. Low angle bevels almost everything, high bevels only very sharp edges.
BevelModifier.vertex_group: Vertex group that decides which vertices or edges get beveled (used by the Vertex Group limit method).
BevelModifier.invert_vertex_group: Flip the vertex group, so painted areas are ignored and unpainted areas are affected.
BevelModifier.use_clamp_overlap: Stops the bevel from growing so large that neighboring bevels overlap and wreck the shape.
BevelModifier.offset_type: What the Width number actually measures.
BevelModifier.offset_type.OFFSET: Width is how far the new edges sit from the original edge.
BevelModifier.offset_type.WIDTH: Width is the width of the new bevel face.
BevelModifier.offset_type.DEPTH: Width is the straight distance from the original edge to the bevel face.
BevelModifier.offset_type.PERCENT: Width is a percent of the length of the neighboring edges.
BevelModifier.offset_type.ABSOLUTE: Width is a fixed distance measured along the neighboring edges.
BevelModifier.profile_type: The shape of the bevel's cross-section: a simple curve or one you draw yourself.
BevelModifier.profile_type.SUPERELLIPSE: A curve you shape with the Shape slider, from concave to convex.
BevelModifier.profile_type.CUSTOM: Draw any curve you like with the profile curve editor.
BevelModifier.profile: Shape of the curve. 0.5 is a perfect round, lower is flatter and sunken, higher is bulged out.
BevelModifier.material: Material slot number for the new bevel faces. -1 means pick automatically from the nearby faces.
BevelModifier.loop_slide: Let the bevel slide along edges to keep it even where meshes meet, instead of forcing equal widths.
BevelModifier.mark_seam: Mark the new bevel edges as UV seams, which controls how the texture unwraps.
BevelModifier.mark_sharp: Mark the new bevel edges as sharp, which gives hard shading lines there.
BevelModifier.harden_normals: Make the shading of the bevel faces match the big flat faces next to them, for clean, crisp shading.
BevelModifier.face_strength_mode: Tags faces with a strength value that custom normals and Weighted Normal use. Choose which faces get it.
BevelModifier.face_strength_mode.FSTR_NEW: Set face strength only on the new bevel faces.
BevelModifier.face_strength_mode.FSTR_AFFECTED: Set face strength on the new faces and the faces they touch.
BevelModifier.face_strength_mode.FSTR_ALL: Set face strength on every face of the mesh.
BevelModifier.miter_outer: What shape the outside of a corner takes where beveled edges meet at an angle.
BevelModifier.miter_outer.MITER_SHARP: The outside of the corner stays a sharp point.
BevelModifier.miter_outer.MITER_PATCH: The outside of the corner is cut into a flat, squared patch.
BevelModifier.miter_outer.MITER_ARC: The outside of the corner is rounded off into an arc.
BevelModifier.miter_inner: What shape the inside of a corner takes where beveled edges meet at an angle.
BevelModifier.miter_inner.MITER_SHARP: The inside of the corner stays a sharp point.
BevelModifier.miter_inner.MITER_ARC: The inside of the corner is rounded off into an arc.
BevelModifier.spread: How far apart the inner arc points are placed. Only matters when Inner Miter is Arc.
BevelModifier.vmesh_method: How the mesh is built where several beveled edges meet at one point.
BevelModifier.vmesh_method.CUTOFF: Cut each profile off at the end and cap it, a simpler, flatter corner.

BooleanModifier.show_in_editmode: Show the modifier's result while you edit the mesh or shape in Edit Mode.

BooleanModifier.show_expanded: Open or fold this modifier's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
BooleanModifier.is_active: Marks this as the modifier you are currently working on in the stack.
BooleanModifier.use_pin_to_last: Keeps this modifier locked at the bottom of the stack, so newly added modifiers go above it.
BooleanModifier.use_apply_on_spline: Applies this modifier, and the deforming ones above it, to the curve's control points instead of the finished shape.
BooleanModifier.operation: What shape math to do between this object and the other one.
BooleanModifier.operation.INTERSECT: Keep only the part where both shapes overlap.
BooleanModifier.operation.DIFFERENCE: Cut the other shape out of this one, like punching a hole.
BooleanModifier.operand_type: Whether the cutter is a single object or a whole collection of objects.
BooleanModifier.operand_type.OBJECT: Use one mesh object as the cutter.
BooleanModifier.operand_type.COLLECTION: Use all mesh objects in a collection as the cutters.
BooleanModifier.double_threshold: How close surfaces must be to count as overlapping. Raise it if you get tiny gaps or glitches. Float solver only.
BooleanModifier.solver: Which calculation method to use. It is a trade-off between speed and accuracy.
BooleanModifier.solver.FLOAT: Fast and simple, but struggles with overlapping or touching faces.
BooleanModifier.solver.EXACT: Slower but most accurate, best when faces sit flat against each other.
BooleanModifier.solver.MANIFOLD: Fastest and clean, but both meshes must be closed solids with no holes.
BooleanModifier.use_self: Allow the mesh to cut into itself where its own parts overlap. Exact solver only.
BooleanModifier.use_hole_tolerant: Gives better results if the meshes have holes or gaps, but is slower. Exact solver only.
BooleanModifier.material_mode: How materials are assigned to the new faces made by the boolean.
BooleanModifier.material_mode.INDEX: Use the same material slot numbers as the original, matching by slot order.
BooleanModifier.material_mode.TRANSFER: Copy materials from both objects over, adding new slots when needed.
BooleanModifier.debug_options: Developer options for finding bugs. They only work when Blender is started with the -d flag.
BooleanModifier.debug_options.SEPARATE: Keep the result pieces as separate parts instead of joining them.
BooleanModifier.debug_options.NO_DISSOLVE: Skip the cleanup step that dissolves unneeded edges.
BooleanModifier.debug_options.NO_CONNECT_REGIONS: Skip connecting the separate regions of the result.

DataTransferModifier.use_poly_data: Transfer data stored on whole faces.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_verts: Which kinds of vertex data to copy.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_verts.VGROUP_WEIGHTS: Copy vertex group weights (the paint that rigs and modifiers use).
DataTransferModifier.data_types_edges: Which kinds of edge data to copy.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_edges.SHARP_EDGE: Copy which edges are marked sharp.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_loops: Which kinds of face-corner data to copy.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_loops.UV: Copy UV maps, which control how textures wrap on the mesh.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_polys: Which kinds of face data to copy.
DataTransferModifier.data_types_polys.SMOOTH: Copy which faces are flat or smooth shaded.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping: How each destination vertex finds its matching source data.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.TOPOLOGY: Match by index, for meshes with exactly the same structure.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.NEAREST: Copy from the closest source vertex.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.EDGE_NEAREST: Copy from the closest vertex of the closest source edge.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.EDGEINTERP_NEAREST: Blend the two ends of the closest source edge, based on the nearest point on it.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.POLY_NEAREST: Copy from the closest vertex of the closest source face.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.POLYINTERP_NEAREST: Blend the corners of the closest source face, based on the nearest point on it.
DataTransferModifier.vert_mapping.POLYINTERP_VNORPROJ: Shoot a ray along the vertex normal and blend the corners of the face it hits.
DataTransferModifier.edge_mapping: How each destination edge finds its matching source data.
DataTransferModifier.edge_mapping.TOPOLOGY: Match by index, for meshes with exactly the same structure.
DataTransferModifier.edge_mapping.VERT_NEAREST: Copy from the source edge whose end points are closest to this edge's end points.
DataTransferModifier.edge_mapping.NEAREST: Copy from the closest source edge, comparing edge midpoints.
DataTransferModifier.edge_mapping.POLY_NEAREST: Copy from the closest edge of the closest source face, comparing midpoints.
DataTransferModifier.edge_mapping.EDGEINTERP_VNORPROJ: Project the edge along its normals and blend all source edges it hits.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping: How each destination face corner finds its matching source data.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping.TOPOLOGY: Match by index, for meshes with exactly the same structure.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping.NEAREST_NORMAL: Copy from the closest corner whose normal points in a similar direction.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping.NEAREST_POLYNOR: Copy from the closest corner whose face normal best matches this face.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping.NEAREST_POLY: Copy from the closest corner of the closest source face.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping.POLYINTERP_NEAREST: Blend the corners of the nearest source face.
DataTransferModifier.loop_mapping.POLYINTERP_LNORPROJ: Project along the corner normal and blend the corners of the source face it hits.
DataTransferModifier.poly_mapping: How each destination face finds its matching source face.
DataTransferModifier.poly_mapping.TOPOLOGY: Match by index, for meshes with exactly the same structure.
DataTransferModifier.poly_mapping.NEAREST: Copy from the closest source face, comparing face centers.
DataTransferModifier.poly_mapping.NORMAL: Copy from the source face whose normal points most like this face.
DataTransferModifier.poly_mapping.POLYINTERP_PNORPROJ: Project the face along its normal and blend all source faces it hits.
DataTransferModifier.use_max_distance: Only copy from source parts that are within Max Distance. Anything farther away is ignored.
DataTransferModifier.max_distance: The farthest a source part may be and still be used. Low is strict, high lets far things match.
DataTransferModifier.ray_radius: How thick the search rays are. Larger rays hit thin things like edges and vertices more easily.
DataTransferModifier.islands_precision: Accuracy when matching UV islands (separate UV pieces). Around 0.1 is fine, higher can fix thin pieces but is slower.
DataTransferModifier.layers_vgroup_select_src: Which of the source layers to copy when there are several (for example several UV maps).
DataTransferModifier.layers_vgroup_select_src.BONE_SELECT: Copy all vertex groups used by the selected pose bones.
DataTransferModifier.layers_vgroup_select_src.BONE_DEFORM: Copy all vertex groups used by deforming bones.
DataTransferModifier.layers_vcol_vert_select_src: Which of the source layers to copy when there are several (for example several UV maps).

DataTransferModifier.layers_vcol_vert_select_src.BONE_DEFORM: Copy all vertex groups used by deforming bones.

DataTransferModifier.layers_vcol_loop_select_src.BONE_SELECT: Copy all vertex groups used by the selected pose bones.
DataTransferModifier.layers_vcol_loop_select_src.BONE_DEFORM: Copy all vertex groups used by deforming bones.

DataTransferModifier.layers_uv_select_src.BONE_SELECT: Copy all vertex groups used by the selected pose bones.
DataTransferModifier.layers_uv_select_src.BONE_DEFORM: Copy all vertex groups used by deforming bones.

DataTransferModifier.layers_vgroup_select_dst.ACTIVE: Write everything into the active layer of the target.
DataTransferModifier.layers_vgroup_select_dst.NAME: Match layers by name, so 'UVMap' goes into 'UVMap'.
DataTransferModifier.layers_vgroup_select_dst.INDEX: Match layers by their order in the list (first to first, second to second).

DataTransferModifier.mix_mode: How the source data affects the data already on the destination.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.REPLACE: Overwrite the destination data with the source data.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.ABOVE_THRESHOLD: Only overwrite where the destination value is above the Mix Factor threshold.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.BELOW_THRESHOLD: Only overwrite where the destination value is below the Mix Factor threshold.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.MIX: Blend source into destination, with Mix Factor as the blend amount.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.ADD: Add the source value to the destination, scaled by Mix Factor.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.SUB: Subtract the source value from the destination, scaled by Mix Factor.
DataTransferModifier.mix_mode.MUL: Multiply the destination by the source value, scaled by Mix Factor.
DataTransferModifier.mix_factor: Strength of the mix. 0 keeps the destination as is, 1 applies the source fully. Also used as a threshold in some modes.
DataTransferModifier.vertex_group: Optional vertex group limiting which parts of this mesh receive data. Empty means everywhere.
DataTransferModifier.invert_vertex_group: Flip the vertex group, so painted areas are skipped and unpainted areas receive data.

DecimateModifier._: Reduces how many faces a mesh has, making it lighter and faster while trying to keep its overall look.
DecimateModifier.show_viewport: Show the modifier's effect in the 3D viewport. Turn it off if the viewport feels slow.
DecimateModifier.show_render: Use the modifier when you render the final image. Off means renders ignore it.
DecimateModifier.show_in_editmode: Show the modifier's result while you edit the mesh or shape in Edit Mode.
DecimateModifier.show_on_cage: Edit Mode only: lets you grab and move the modified result directly instead of the original points.
DecimateModifier.show_expanded: Open or fold this modifier's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
DecimateModifier.is_active: Marks this as the modifier you are currently working on in the stack.
DecimateModifier.use_pin_to_last: Keeps this modifier locked at the bottom of the stack, so newly added modifiers go above it.
DecimateModifier.use_apply_on_spline: Applies this modifier, and the deforming ones above it, to the curve's control points instead of the finished shape.
DecimateModifier.decimate_type: Which method is used to cut down the face count.
DecimateModifier.decimate_type.COLLAPSE: Merge edges together, step by step, until the target ratio is reached.
DecimateModifier.decimate_type.UNSUBDIV: Reverse subdivision by removing the extra detail, best for meshes made by subdividing.
DecimateModifier.decimate_type.DISSOLVE: Merge flat neighboring faces into bigger flat faces, without changing the shape.
DecimateModifier.ratio: How much of the face count to keep. 1 keeps everything, 0.5 keeps about half, near 0 leaves very few. Collapse only.
DecimateModifier.iterations: How many times to undo subdivision. Each step removes one level of detail. Un-Subdivide only.
DecimateModifier.angle_limit: Faces are merged only if the angle between them is smaller than this. Higher merges more. Planar only.
DecimateModifier.vertex_group: Vertex group that protects parts of the mesh from being reduced. Collapse only.
DecimateModifier.invert_vertex_group: Flip the vertex group, so painted areas are reduced and unpainted areas stay safe. Collapse only.
DecimateModifier.use_collapse_triangulate: Keep the result as triangles instead of letting Blender turn them back into quads. Collapse only.
DecimateModifier.use_symmetry: Keep the reduction mirrored on one axis, so left and right stay matching.
DecimateModifier.symmetry_axis: Which axis the symmetry is mirrored across.
DecimateModifier.vertex_group_factor: How strongly the vertex group protects the mesh. Higher means more of the painted part is kept.
DecimateModifier.use_dissolve_boundaries: Also dissolve points along the edges of the mesh's open borders. Planar only.
DecimateModifier.delimit: Things that stop faces from being merged, so these details survive.
DecimateModifier.delimit.NORMAL: Don't merge faces that face different directions.
DecimateModifier.delimit.MATERIAL: Don't merge faces that use different materials.

DisplaceModifier.use_apply_on_spline: Applies this modifier, and the deforming ones above it, to the curve's control points instead of the finished shape.

DisplaceModifier.strength: How far points move. Low gives subtle bumps, high gives deep ones. Negative flips the direction.
DisplaceModifier.direction.X: Push along the X axis, based on the texture brightness.
DisplaceModifier.direction.Y: Push along the Y axis, based on the texture brightness.
DisplaceModifier.direction.Z: Push along the Z axis, based on the texture brightness.
DisplaceModifier.direction.NORMAL: Push along each point's normal (straight out of the surface).
DisplaceModifier.direction.CUSTOM_NORMAL: Push along the averaged custom normals.
DisplaceModifier.direction.RGB_TO_XYZ: Use the texture's red, green and blue values as the X, Y and Z push amounts.
DisplaceModifier.space: Whether the push direction is measured in the object's own axes or the world axes.
DisplaceModifier.invert_vertex_group: Flip the vertex group, so painted areas are ignored and unpainted areas are affected.
DisplaceModifier.texture_coords: How the texture is placed on the mesh.
DisplaceModifier.texture_coords.GLOBAL: Use world coordinates, so the pattern stays fixed in space as the object moves.
DisplaceModifier.texture_coords.OBJECT: Use the coordinates of another object, which you can move to slide the texture around.
DisplaceModifier.texture_coords.UV: Use the mesh's UV map, so the texture follows the unwrapped layout.
DisplaceModifier.uv_layer: Which UV map to use when Texture Coordinates is set to UV.
DisplaceModifier.texture_coords_bone: The bone whose position places the texture, when the texture coordinates come from an armature object.

FloorConstraint._: Stops the owner from passing through the target, like a floor, wall or ceiling, so it can sit on top of it.
FloorConstraint.owner_space: Which coordinate system the constrained object (the owner) is measured in. World is the scene grid, Local is the object's own axes.
FloorConstraint.owner_space.WORLD: Use the world grid, the same for every object in the scene.
FloorConstraint.owner_space.CUSTOM: Use the axes of another object, bone or vertex group that you pick.
FloorConstraint.owner_space.POSE: Armature bones only: use the pose space and ignore the armature object's own move/rotate/scale.
FloorConstraint.owner_space.LOCAL_WITH_PARENT: Bones: local to the bone's rest pose, but still including whatever its parent adds.
FloorConstraint.owner_space.LOCAL: Use the owner's own axes, so 'X' means along the object's own X direction.
FloorConstraint.target_space: Which coordinate system the target is read in. This decides what 'the target's X' means before it is copied or used.
FloorConstraint.target_space.WORLD: Read the target using the world grid.
FloorConstraint.target_space.CUSTOM: Read the target using the axes of another object, bone or vertex group you pick.
FloorConstraint.target_space.POSE: Armature bones only: read the target in pose space and ignore the armature object's own transform.
FloorConstraint.target_space.LOCAL_WITH_PARENT: Bones: read the target in its rest-pose local space, still including its parent's effect.
FloorConstraint.target_space.LOCAL: Read the target using its own axes.
FloorConstraint.target_space.LOCAL_OWNER_ORIENT: Local space plus a fix for the owner and target bones resting at different angles, so they move the same way.
FloorConstraint.space_subtarget: The bone, or vertex group, whose axes are used when a Custom space is chosen. Leave empty to use the object itself.
FloorConstraint.mute: Switch this constraint off without deleting it. Handy for quickly seeing what it does.
FloorConstraint.enabled: Turns the constraint's result on or off. Off means Blender ignores it completely.
FloorConstraint.show_expanded: Open or fold this constraint's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
FloorConstraint.active: Marks this as the constraint you are currently editing in the stack.
FloorConstraint.influence: How strongly the constraint applies. 0 means no effect, 1 means full effect, in between blends the two.
FloorConstraint.subtarget: The specific bone, or vertex group, on the target to use. Leave empty to use the whole target object.
FloorConstraint.floor_location: Which side of the target counts as the floor, and which direction the owner is blocked from passing.
FloorConstraint.floor_location.FLOOR_X: The target's +X side is the floor; the owner cannot go past it.
FloorConstraint.floor_location.FLOOR_Y: The target's +Y side is the floor; the owner cannot go past it.
FloorConstraint.floor_location.FLOOR_Z: The target's +Z side is the floor; the owner cannot go past it.
FloorConstraint.floor_location.FLOOR_NEGATIVE_X: The target's -X side is the floor; the owner cannot go past it.
FloorConstraint.floor_location.FLOOR_NEGATIVE_Y: The target's -Y side is the floor; the owner cannot go past it.
FloorConstraint.floor_location.FLOOR_NEGATIVE_Z: The target's -Z side is the floor; the owner cannot go past it.
FloorConstraint.use_rotation: Use the target's rotation to decide the direction of the floor. Off means it always uses the world axes.
FloorConstraint.offset: Moves the floor away from the target's origin. Positive keeps the owner higher above the floor.

GeometryAttributeConstraint._: Moves the owner to a transform stored in a geometry attribute (data on points, edges, faces, etc.) of the target object.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.owner_space: Which coordinate system the constrained object (the owner) is measured in. World is the scene grid, Local is the object's own axes.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.owner_space.WORLD: Use the world grid, the same for every object in the scene.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.owner_space.CUSTOM: Use the axes of another object, bone or vertex group that you pick.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.owner_space.POSE: Armature bones only: use the pose space and ignore the armature object's own move/rotate/scale.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.owner_space.LOCAL_WITH_PARENT: Bones: local to the bone's rest pose, but still including whatever its parent adds.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.owner_space.LOCAL: Use the owner's own axes, so 'X' means along the object's own X direction.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space: Which coordinate system the target is read in. This decides what 'the target's X' means before it is copied or used.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space.WORLD: Read the target using the world grid.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space.CUSTOM: Read the target using the axes of another object, bone or vertex group you pick.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space.POSE: Armature bones only: read the target in pose space and ignore the armature object's own transform.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space.LOCAL_WITH_PARENT: Bones: read the target in its rest-pose local space, still including its parent's effect.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space.LOCAL: Read the target using its own axes.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.target_space.LOCAL_OWNER_ORIENT: Local space plus a fix for the owner and target bones resting at different angles, so they move the same way.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.space_subtarget: The bone, or vertex group, whose axes are used when a Custom space is chosen. Leave empty to use the object itself.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mute: Switch this constraint off without deleting it. Handy for quickly seeing what it does.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.enabled: Turns the constraint's result on or off. Off means Blender ignores it completely.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.show_expanded: Open or fold this constraint's panel in the Properties editor. Only changes how it looks in the UI, not what it does.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.active: Marks this as the constraint you are currently editing in the stack.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.influence: How strongly the constraint applies. 0 means no effect, 1 means full effect, in between blends the two.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.attribute_name: Name of the attribute that holds the transform to use.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.domain: Which part of the geometry holds the attribute.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.domain.INSTANCE: Stored on instances (copies placed by Geometry Nodes).
GeometryAttributeConstraint.apply_target_transform: Also apply the target object's own position, rotation and scale on top of the attribute's transform.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.data_type: What kind of data the attribute holds, which decides what part of the transform it controls.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.data_type.QUATERNION: A rotation value, which controls rotation.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.data_type.FLOAT4X4: A full 4x4 matrix, which controls position, rotation and scale together.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.sample_index: Which element (point, edge, face, ...) of the attribute to read, counting from 0.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_loc: Apply the location from the attribute.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_rot: Apply the rotation from the attribute.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_scl: Apply the scale from the attribute.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_mode: How the transform from the attribute is combined with the owner's existing transform.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_mode.REPLACE: Throw away the owner's transform and use the attribute's.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_mode.BEFORE_FULL: Attribute transform goes first, then the owner's, combined as plain full matrices.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_mode.BEFORE_SPLIT: Attribute transform goes first, but location, rotation and scale are each combined separately.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_mode.AFTER_FULL: Owner's transform goes first, then the attribute's, combined as plain full matrices.
GeometryAttributeConstraint.mix_mode.AFTER_SPLIT: Attribute transform goes after, but location, rotation and scale are each combined separately.

GreasePencilBuildModifier.mode: How the strokes of a drawing are built up.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.mode.SEQUENTIAL: Strokes appear one after another, only one changing at a time.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.mode.ADDITIVE: Only builds strokes that are new, for drawings made by adding to the last frame.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.transition: Whether the strokes grow in, shrink away or fade out.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.transition.GROW: Strokes draw themselves from start to end.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.transition.SHRINK: Strokes disappear from their end back to their start.

GreasePencilBuildModifier.concurrent_time_alignment.END: All strokes end together, so short ones start later.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.time_mode: How the speed of the build is decided.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.time_mode.DRAWSPEED: Use the speed you originally drew at, times a factor.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.time_mode.FRAMES: Use a fixed number of frames for every build.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.time_mode.PERCENTAGE: Set by hand how much of the stroke is built.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.speed_factor: Multiplies your recorded drawing speed. 2 builds twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.speed_maxgap: The longest pause between strokes, in seconds. Longer pauses from when you drew are shortened to this.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.use_restrict_frame_range: Only build strokes during the chosen frame range, leaving other frames untouched.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.use_percentage: Control how many points are visible with a percentage instead of time.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.percentage_factor: How much of each stroke is visible. 0 is nothing, 1 is all of it.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.frame_start: First frame of the range where the effect works.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.frame_end: Last frame of the range where the effect works.
GreasePencilBuildModifier.use_fading: Fade strokes out softly instead of cutting them off sharply.

GreasePencilLengthModifier.seed: Changes the random pattern. Try different numbers for different results.

GreasePencilLengthModifier.overshoot_factor: How much of the stroke is used to work out the direction of the extension.

GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_clip_plane_boundaries: Show lines created where the camera's near or far clipping plane slices through objects.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.crease_threshold: Angles smaller than this count as creases. Lower catches only sharp folds, higher catches softer ones.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.split_angle: Strokes are cut in two where the angle on screen is sharper than this. Helps with kinks.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.smooth_tolerance: How much jagged chains are smoothed. Higher gives smoother lines but can lose detail.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_loose_as_contour: Treat loose edges (edges with no face) as contour lines.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.invert_source_vertex_group: Flip the source vertex group, so painted areas are skipped and unpainted areas are traced.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_output_vertex_group_match_by_name: Match the output vertex group to the source one by name.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_face_mark: Filter feature lines using Freestyle face marks.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_face_mark_boundaries: Filter lines using the borders of marked face areas.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_face_mark_keep_contour: Keep contour lines even when the face mark filter would remove them.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.chaining_image_threshold: Line pieces closer than this on screen get joined into one chain. Higher joins more.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_loose_edge_chain: Allow loose edges to be joined into chains.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_geometry_space_chain: Measure chaining distance in 3D space instead of on the screen image.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_detail_preserve: Keep the small zig-zag noise from the first chaining step, instead of smoothing it away.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_overlap_edge_type_support: Let an edge have several line types at once, and make a separate stroke for each.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.stroke_depth_offset: Nudges the strokes slightly toward the camera so they don't get hidden inside the surface.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_offset_towards_custom_camera: Nudge strokes toward the chosen custom camera instead of the active camera.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.source_type: Where the objects to trace come from.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.source_type.COLLECTION: Trace all objects in a collection.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_contour: Draw outlines where an object's silhouette meets the background.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_loose: Draw lines for loose edges (edges not part of a face).
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_crease: Draw lines on sharp creases and folds.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_material: Draw lines where two different materials meet.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_edge_mark: Draw lines on edges that you marked with Freestyle.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_intersection: Draw lines where objects cut through each other.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_light_contour: Draw lines between the lit and shaded parts, based on a reference light object.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_shadow: Draw the outline of cast shadows, projected from a light object.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_region_filtering: Keep only lines from lit or shaded regions. Does not affect cast shadow and light contour lines.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_region_filtering.ILLUMINATED: Keep only lines from lit regions.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_region_filtering.SHADED: Keep only lines from shaded regions.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_region_filtering.ILLUMINATED_ENCL: Keep lines from lit regions, plus the lines enclosing them (contour, light contour and shadow).
GreasePencilLineartModifier.silhouette_filtering: Choose which contour lines to keep, based on silhouettes.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.silhouette_filtering.GROUP: Keep silhouettes of collections or groups.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.silhouette_filtering.INDIVIDUAL: Keep the silhouette of each single object.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.fill_strokes: Make filled shapes instead of only outlines.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_multiple_levels: Draw lines from a range of occlusion levels, meaning hidden behind that many surfaces.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.level_start: Fewest surfaces a line may be hidden behind to be drawn. 0 means fully visible lines.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.level_end: Most surfaces a line may be hidden behind to be drawn. Higher shows more hidden lines.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.target_layer: The Grease Pencil layer that receives the generated strokes.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.source_vertex_group: Only trace mesh vertex groups whose names start with this text. Empty traces all.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.vertex_group: Vertex group assigned to the generated strokes.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.is_baked: Shows whether this modifier already has its strokes baked (saved), so it no longer recalculates.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_cache: Reuse the scene data from the first Line Art modifier above, which is faster but locks some settings.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.overscan: Extra margin beyond the image edge so strokes don't stop abruptly at the border.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.radius: Thickness of the generated strokes. Low is thin, high is thick.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.opacity: How solid the generated strokes are. 0 is invisible, 1 is fully solid.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_material_mask: Use material masks to hide lines that are blocked by other materials.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_material_mask_match: Require all selected material masks to match, instead of just one.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_material_mask_bits: Which material mask bits to match, set in the materials' Line Art settings.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_intersection_match: Require all selected intersection masks to match, instead of just one.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_intersection_mask: Which collection mask bits to match, set in the collections' Line Art settings.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_crease_on_smooth: Allow crease lines to show on smooth surfaces.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_crease_on_sharp: Allow crease lines to show on edges that are already sharp.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_image_boundary_trimming: Cut all lines exactly at the image border, including the overscan area.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_back_face_culling: Ignore faces pointing away from the camera to save time. Can change which occlusion levels show up.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_camera_near: Closest distance the shadow camera sees. Things nearer than this are cut off.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_camera_far: Farthest distance the shadow camera sees. Things beyond this are cut off.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.shadow_camera_size: Size of the shadow camera's view (its orthographic scale). Bigger covers more area.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_invert_collection: Select everything except the lines from the chosen collection.
GreasePencilLineartModifier.use_invert_silhouette: Select the opposite of silhouette lines, the lines inside the shape.

GreasePencilTextureModifier.fit_method: How the texture is stretched along each stroke.

GreasePencilTextureModifier.fit_method.FIT_STROKE: Stretch the texture to fit the full length of each stroke.

GreasePencilThickModifierData.use_weight_factor: Use vertex group weights to control how strongly the thickness changes.
GreasePencilThickModifierData.use_uniform_thickness: Replace the thickness with one value, instead of scaling each point's own thickness.
